methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Signaloid is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Phillip Stanley-Marbell that has raised $10M to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 identifiable private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or valuation-tier clustering to support a reliable peer-median analysis—only one adjacent-stage comparable exists within narrow filters, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold for statistical validity.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable here. Using the $10M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next stage yields an implied valuation of $25M. Public-Comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be executed because Signaloid's revenue is not disclosed, as is standard for private companies at this stage. The Semiconductors public median trades at 21.0x sales, but without revenue data, this multiple cannot be applied to establish a floor or ceiling.

The analysis supports a range of $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. This estimate carries material uncertainty due to reliance on a single applicable method and the absence of private-peer valuation density in the near-term funding window. Key unknowns include the company's current run-rate, gross margins, and competitive positioning relative to its named peers—factors that typically drive seed-extension rounds in semiconductors.
